content:
I have a reproducible memory Lean on v4.34.0-rc1 on Windows.

The way I can reproduce it:

  • Open the task manager
  • clone and open https://github.com/riccardobrasca/LFTCM2026/blob/master/LFTCM2026/6_AlgebraNumberTheory.lean in VSCode
  • repeatedly insert/delete an empty line on line 25 (briefly waiting for the file to compile).
  • Every time I do, lean.exe uses 20MB more than before.

I'll try to minimize, but I'm currently in a location with really slow internet, so it might take a while.

I can reproduce much more easily:

  • In an empty Lean file(!), repeatedly add a new line and remove it.
  • This will (much more slowly) increase the memory usage every time (~2 MB per change)

So it doesn't depend on Mathlib at all. (though it might depend on the project-specific options from the project above)
Can someone on Linux confirm that the memory leak doesn't exist there?
Note: lean.exe is a separate process than VSCode (not sure if that is what it's supposed to be)

I tried it out (as described in your first message), and I can indeed reproduce it on Windows. I kept going to see what would happen when I ran out of memory, and I got this error:

failed to create thread: 1455
I have also gotten that. My OS has also crashed other times. I'm now running on WSL; there is no memory leak there.
I have never bothered to really profile it but sometimes using lean I have to forcefully shut down the PC because of multiple edits. On Linux.
This happens to me too, but I realized it was because the swap partition is full or something similar. I've installed earlyoom and the problem is solved.
I guess it's pretty much the same in rc2. I've got multiple oom crashes in my vscode (windows) which never happened before switching the toolchain version.
Thanks for the clear report, tracked down and fixed in lean4#15060
